tldr: A small principal-stratum share can leave observed mediator and outcome channels strong while its covariate composition is weakly observed. The contribution is a purely theoretical finite-tuple precision benchmark for an already identified principal natural indirect effect under newly maintained independent-uniform structural errors and fixed public class restrictions. On the complete primitive class, total estimators and explicitly calibrated honest intervals attain the full all-rule risk and length frontier: the original-record root scale is \(\min\{1,\max\{(n\delta^2)^{-1/2},(n\delta)^{-2/7}\}\}\), while supplying the composition gives \(n^{-2/7}\). This identifies saturation at \(\delta=n^{-1/2}\), the unequal-channel crossover at \(\delta=n^{-3/10}\), equality of risk-root and honest-length orders, and the explicit price of learning composition. A derived published-denominator diagnostic explains why fixed-law first-order inference does not supply shrinking-mass control. No substantive cross-world-independence regime or observational-data precision guarantee is asserted.
